Here are three recent papers on evaluating RAG systems. I picked them from search-result snippets and haven't read the full papers.

1. **RAGStress** (arXiv 2610.04691, Oct 2026). It's a controlled benchmark that evaluates RAG when the knowledge base is degraded.
2. **EnterpriseRAG-Bench** (arXiv 2605.05253, May 2026). It's a benchmark for company-internal knowledge, with a 500,000-document synthetic corpus spanning nine enterprise source types. It has 500 questions across ten categories.
3. **Legal RAG Bench** (arXiv 2603.01710, Mar 2026). It's a benchmark and evaluation methodology for the end-to-end performance of legal RAG systems.

Other recent candidates from the same search include:
- RAGPerf (2603.10765), which profiles the system behavior of RAG pipelines.
- The RAT, a Bayesian evaluation model (2608.24753). The snippet I got for it only showed a reference list, so I couldn't confirm what it does.

- [Legal RAG Bench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01710)
- [RAGPerf](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.10765v1)
- [The RAT](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.24753)
